content: It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to ensure proper monitoring and management of your treatment. If you miss a dose of this medication, it is critical to follow specific instructions based on the type of dose missed: Missed Injection: Contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Missed Inhaled Dose: Use the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. For those using colistimethate as an inhalation: Store unmixed vials at room temperature. Do not use premixed solutions or prepare the solution in advance, as this increases the risk of severe respiratory complications. Always prepare the inhalation solution immediately before use. Discard any unused solution after 24 hours. Do not store it for longer periods. Proper storage of this medication is crucial: Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, following local disposal guidelines or consulting your pharmacist. This information was last revised in May 2024. Important Notes on Usage: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific condition. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this medication and your individual health needs. Uses: Colistimethate is an antibiotic used to treat specific bacterial infections. How to Use: For injection, colistimethate is typically administered into a vein or muscle as directed by your doctor. If you are administering this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly trained by your healthcare provider on preparation and usage. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. If inhaling this medication, learn how to properly prepare the solution and use the nebulizer machine. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return. Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset and itching. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using colistimethate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, polymyxin B, colistin, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Colistimethate may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function) should be conducted while using this medication to monitor for potential side effects and ensure its effectiveness. Always keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
